summary:
ASTRO LAB: Interactive 3D Spaceflight & Astronomy Simulator

What We Developed:
We created ASTRO LAB, a zero-dependency, open-source 3D space exploration and astronautics simulation game that runs directly in any modern web browser. Powered by Three.js and vanilla JavaScript, it features a 7-stage astronaut training career campaign, a full-scale 3D solar system driven by real J2000 orbital parameters, 11 lunar surface landing expeditions with low-gravity physics, and six interactive astrophysical simulation labs.
How It Addresses the Challenge:
Typical space training is usually associated with abstract concepts of mathematics and static diagrams. ASTRO LAB overcomes this problem by transforming authentic NASA planetary data and maps from LRO into experiential learning. Trainees are not only familiarized with the concepts of Hohmann transfer, Tsiolkovsky rocket dynamics, and lunar geology, but they also calculate the delta-v budget, build life-support systems, and get knowledgeable about rovers in specific landing sites.
Why It Is Important:
Accessibility is at the core of ASTRO LAB. By embedding procedural textures, real moon maps, and 3D assets into a single lightweight build, the simulator requires no heavy downloads, external servers, or high-end GPUs. It democratizes aerospace science, empowering students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide—even in offline and low-bandwidth environments—to experience spaceflight firsthand.
details: 1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?ASTRO LAB is a browser-based 3D spaceflight simulator and astronomy learning engine. It works through four integrated parts:* Career Campaign: Players start as an astronaut candidate. Go through seven immersive chapters, including training in a neutral buoyancy pool, emergency fire and CO2 scrubber drills, space greenhouse maintenance, 6-DOF Canadarm robotics operations, and launch/orbit burns.* 3D Solar System Engine: It shows the Sun, eight planets, dwarf planets like Ceres and Pluto, and ten major moons. The positions and orbits of these bodies are calculated using real data from the J2000 epoch.* Surface Expeditions: It takes players to 11 landing sites such as Apollo 11 Tranquility Base and Shackleton Crater with correct gravity, low-gravity movement, terrain raycasting, and a Lunar Roving Vehicle.* Interactive Physics Labs: Players do experiments showing the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Hohmann transfer orbits, N-body gravitational assists, exoplanetary habitability, telescope diffraction limits, and black hole gravitational lensing.2. What Benefits Does It Have?* Active Experiential Learning: Instead of reading charts, users change orbits and do real experiments like the Galileo hammer-and-feather drop.* Zero Barrier to Entry: It runs in any browser on desktops, Chromebooks, tablets, or phones without needing installs, app stores, or browser extensions.* 100% Offline Resilience: It works without internet or servers because it uses shaders and embedded maps, making it good for rural areas and remote places.* Progress Retention: It saves XP, ranks, mission logs, and badges on the device using storage that handles corruption and keeps data safe.3. What Is the Intended Impact?The goal is to make aerospace and astrophysics education available to everyone. By turning NASA data into a fun simulator, ASTRO LAB wants to inspire scientists, engineers, and astronauts. It is a ready-to-use lab for teachers who don't have expensive equipment or software.4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used* Languages & Standards: JavaScript (ES2020 Modules) HTML5 Canvas 2D, CSS3 (Modern Glassmorphism UI and custom properties).* 3D & Graphics Engine: Three.js (WebGL rendering, raycasting, custom shaders).* Asset Optimization & Tooling: Python 3 (`build.py` for bundling and Base64 GLB embedding), `esbuild` for JavaScript.*. Quality Assurance: Node.js tests, Playwright for checking devices.* Hardware: Developed on computers; works at 60 FPS on integrated GPUs and mobile devices.5. How Is Your Project Creative?* Narrative Integration with Hard Science: We mixed physics with stories showing astronaut training through real problems like light sensitivity and teamwork.* Procedural-First Asset Design: We made surfaces and atmospheres using math in shaders to save space and speed.* First-Person Tactile Interaction in the Browser: We built hands and physics for picking up items and using switches in 3D.6. What Key Factors Did Our Team Consider?* Scientific Authenticity vs. Playability: Data comes from NASA and LRO. We use HUD tools to show real sizes when needed.*. Universal Design: It has keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad support, subtitles, adjustable text, high contrast, and reduced motion settings.* Low-End Hardware Optimization: It has detail levels and fallback geometry so people without good graphics can still play.
